answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-backed identity with a signed hardware heartbeat. Each agent locks a bond from a unique funding source and signs proofs from one device key; two aliases sharing that key, or even an ember of the same deposit, are slashed and lose the bond. Payouts use a quadratic rule, so an attacker cannot wander a stake across many fake nodes for extra reward, yet still pays a fresh bond and attestation fee per alias. Minting N identities costs N bonds plus N distinct keys, a saffron price far above what those fakes could ever earn.
